name: Ramp
text:
Add a **large, high-contrast skip link** at the top of every page, visible by default.

This ensures keyboard users can bypass repetitive navigation blocks instantly, fixing a core keyboard accessibility failure. The trade-off is minimal screen space, but the benefit for users who rely on keyboard navigation outweighs the cost.

name: Reader
text: A large, always-visible skip link steals focus from the main content for sighted mouse users who don’t need it, creating a new annoyance. Instead, place a subtle but discoverable skip link that only appears on keyboard focus—then test with first-time keyboard users to confirm they notice it without training. The deciding test: if 90% of untrained keyboard users reach the main content in under 5 seconds, the design works.
